questions.title: Explain how checksums detect accidental data corruption
questions.summary: Describe how a checksum helps a system detect that stored or transmitted data has been altered accidentally.
questions.expectation: A strong answer explains what a checksum is, when it is computed, what happens on mismatch, and why that indicates corruption rather than malicious attack.
questions.practicePrompt: Explain how checksums are used to detect accidental corruption when moving a large backup file between two servers.

examMetadata.stimulus: A network administrator moves a large backup file between two servers.

points: checksum value is generated before or during transfer
receiving system recalculates or compares the value
mismatch indicates accidental corruption or an altered file
answer links the check to backup-file integrity
indicativeMarkScheme.modelAnswerOutline: A strong answer explains how the checksum is generated, compared after transfer, and used to flag accidental corruption.
